SUMMARY

Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.(REGN+12.93%)reported third-quarter results characterized by record revenue and earnings growth, driven by the strong commercial performance of its core brands and a strategic expansion of its partnership with Sanofi. Management reported that Dupixent, EYLEA HD, and Libtayo each reached all-time highs in quarterly net sales, while the company also recorded its full share of Sanofi collaboration profits following the repayment of its development balance. The updated Sanofi alliance involves the development of four next-generation long-acting antibodies, for which Regeneron will receive a 1 billion dollar upfront payment in the fourth quarter. The company also detailed clinical advancements in its genetic medicines pipeline, specifically highlighting liver fat reduction data in metabolic disease and promising results for its bispecific antibody in ovarian cancer.

Operator:Welcome to the Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Third Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call. My name is Shannon, and I will be your operator for today's call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. Later, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. Please note that this conference call is being recorded. Ryan Crowe:Thank you, Shannon. Good morning, good afternoon, and good evening to everyone listening around the world. Thank you for your interest in Regeneron, and welcome to our third quarter 2020 earnings conference call. An archive and transcript of this call will be available on the Regeneron Investor Relations website shortly after our call concludes. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Leonard S. Schleifer, cofounder, board cochair, president and chief executive officer, Dr. George D. Yancopoulos, cofounder, board cochair, president, and chief scientific officer, Marion McCourt, executive vice president, commercial and Christopher R. Fenimore, executive vice president finance, and chief financial officer.

For our call today, Len will briefly review key third quarter performance drivers and highlight a few emerging pipeline programs. George will then detail our recent pipeline progress. Followed by Marion, who will review our commercial performance. And finally, Christopher will discuss our financial results and outlook. After our prepared remarks, the remaining time will be available for Q&A. I would like to remind you that remarks made on today's call may include forward-looking statements about Regeneron.

Once our call concludes, the IR team will be available to answer any further questions. With that, let me turn the call over to our president and Chief Executive, Dr. Leonard S. Schleifer.

Leonard S. Schleifer:Thank you, Ryan, and welcome to everyone joining our call today. We are pleased to report another quarter of strong performance. Driven by outstanding commercial execution and a large and diverse pipeline that is continuing to deliver on its promise. Total revenue grew 36% and non GAAP earnings per share grew 70% compared to the third quarter of 2025. This marks our third consecutive quarter of double digit growth on both the top and bottom lines. Our commercial teams continue to execute at a very high level. Dupixent, EYLEA HD, and Libtayo each set new all time highs for quarterly net sales for the second quarter in a row.

DUPIXENT global net sales in the third quarter as reported by Sanofi reached a record $6.5 billion up 35% year over year at constant currency. Which is truly remarkable for a medicine approaching 10 years on the market. In The US, where Dupixent is the leading biologic in 8 of its 9 approved. FDA approved indications, quarterly net sales grew 40% to $5 billion for the first time. Primarily driven by robust demand across all indications as well as gross to net favorability as disclosed by Sanofi. EYLEA HD quarterly net sales in the U.S. reached a new all time high of approximately $700 million up 62% from a year ago.

And now represent nearly 2/3 of our US retinal franchise. Physician unit demand grew 20% sequentially, reflecting the value retinal specialists and their patients see in extended dosing intervals as well as last year's label enhancements, which added the retinal vein occlusion and greater dosing flexibility. We remain optimistic for approval of the prefilled syringe before the end of the year, and we expect it to drive even further adoption if approved. Libtayo is making important differences for patients with skin and lung cancers and it continues to build clinical and commercial momentum. The US, it is the leading immunotherapy in non melanoma skin cancers and the second most prescribed immunotherapy in non small cell lung cancer.

Global net sales reached a record $550 million up 51% in constant currency, and US net sales grew 81% to nearly $400 million. Last week at ESMO, we presented long-term data from our Phase III c-POST trial. Showing an increasing overall survival benefit with adjuvant Libtayo in high risk cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma. Where it is the first and only approved immunotherapy. Libtayo is now on an annual run rate of approximately $2.2 billion and remains the foundation for our broader oncology strategy. Beyond our strong commercial execution, our pipeline is poised to deliver several potential blockbuster opportunities over the next several years.

Let me highlight new advances in 4 of our pipeline programs while George will discuss these in more detail along with other late stage clinical programs. Including Factor XI, lynozyfic, olatorepatide. In neuromuscular disease, we expect an FDA decision in November for cemdisiran in generalized myasthenia gravis. If approved, cemdisiran would be the first siRNA therapy for generalized myasthenia gravis and the only treatment that can offer quarterly subcutaneous dosing. Early in my career as a neurologist, I cared for many patients with this difficult to treat condition, So it is particularly gratifying to see us bring forward a potential new treatment option for them. In metabolic disease, NASH affects millions of people and treatment options are limited.

Our CIDEB program is a great example of our genetics driven scientific process. Regeneron Genetics Center discovered that people with naturally occurring loss-of-function variants of the CIDEB gene have a markedly lower risk of fatty liver disease and cirrhosis. Which led us to develop a first in class siRNA that targets CIDEB. We are encouraged by the initial clinical data which suggests best in class best in disease potential, and we are rapidly advancing this program into registration enabling studies. I would also like to highlight our program for postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome or POTS.

This is an increasingly recognized debilitating condition that affects many young people often disrupting school, work, and daily life, with very few effective treatment options and no FDA approved medicine. Recent estimates suggest that between 500 thousand and several million people in the U.S. alone suffer from POTS. We believe the initial clinical data that George will highlight supports our antibodies potential to become the first FDA approved treatment for this disease, and we plan to initiate a potentially pivotal study next year pending regulatory feedback. In oncology, we recently shared encouraging data for the ubamatamab our MUC16xCD3 bispecific antibody in advanced low grade serous ovarian carcinoma.

This is a rare and difficult to treat form of ovarian cancer that often affects younger women who urgently need better treatment options. We saw durable responses in heavily pretreated patients at rates well above those historically seen with available therapies. We are already enrolling a dedicated potentially registrational cohort and plan to start a confirmatory phase 3 study next year. Each of these programs is supported by compelling clinical data, human genetic validation, or both. It is no accident that they span 4 distinct therapeutic areas and that each has first in class or best in disease potential. That reflects our disease agnostic enterprise approach to R&D.

Rather than confining ourselves to a few therapeutic areas, we apply our core technologies wherever the science leads us. These technology platforms, including our VelocImmune antibody and bispecific engines, Regeneron Genetics Center, and siRNA and gene editing technologies that allow us to translate genetic discoveries like CIDEB into potential medicines. Today, that approach supports approximately 50 clinical programs spanning immunology, oncology, ophthalmology, hematology, cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, neurology, and rare diseases. Our commercial organization has been built the same way. Our teams already call on ophthalmologists, dermatologists, pulmonologists, allergists, gastroenterologists, ENT specialists, oncologists, cardiologists, and hematologists. And if cemtosiran is approved, we will begin to call on neurologists as well.

That means many of our pipeline medicines, including several of the programs I just mentioned, can launch into specialties where we already have deep relationships and expertise and can leverage our existing infrastructure and capabilities. Briefly on business development. Historically, we have been a net out licenser of innovation. With the most recent example being the expansion of our alliance with Sanofi, contributing to the alliance for next generation long acting antibodies, all invented at Regeneron that target the same pathways that made Dupixent so successful. Regeneron will lead research and development, and Sanofi will lead global commercialization now with greater transparency and increased participation by Regeneron.

If approved, these medicines can also benefit from Dupixent's commercial leadership and the strong market access position it has established advantage neither company could capture on its own. At the same time, our financial strength positions us to bring differentiated external innovation into Regeneron. We have done this effectively to date, primarily through early stage research collaborations, including those that built our emerging genetic medicines pipeline across siRNA therapeutics, gene therapy, and gene editing. Continue to evaluate a wide range of opportunities. from early clinical programs and platforms to commercial stage products with a sharp focus on valuation and strategic fit. In closing, this was an exceptional quarter by every measure.

Our 3 core growth brands are performing at record levels. And our expanded alliance with Sanofi positions us to lead the next era of type 2 inflammation medicines. Our pipeline is poised to deliver additional potential blockbusters across a broad range of diseases, and our commercial organization is built to bring them to patients. Our future is bright, and we remain focused on translating our science into new medicines that can make a meaningful difference for patients and create long term value for shareholders. With that, let me turn the call over to George.

George D. Yancopoulos:Thanks, Len. For my remarks today, I will first provide further details on the 4 programs that Len highlighted. Then cover other key updates from our pipeline. Beginning with our c 5 program, regulatory submissions are under review for cemdisiran, our c 5 siRNA, for generalized myasthenia gravis or gMG. An FDA decision is expected next month, and a European Commission decision is anticipated in the second half of 27. If approved, Cemdisiran will be the first and only siRNA therapy approved for gMG. Would be distinguished by a combination of rapid onset consistent efficacy, throughout the dosing interval, manageable safety, and convenient subcutaneous dosing just 4x per year.

Our c 5 program also includes a co formulation of cemdisiran with pozolimab. Our c 5 antibody that is already FDA approved for protein losing enteropathy. Together, they are being evaluated as a combination therapy for paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria or PNH. Where we expect to report pivotal results by the end of the year. Initial results from a lead-in cohort of the phase 3 trial suggest that our novel combination approach could provide best in class control of intravascular hemolysis. Our c 5 program further includes evaluating cemdisiran with and without pozolimab in geographic atrophy or GA. Via systemic administration.

We now expect to report interim 26 week data from an exploratory cohort of our ongoing Phase II/III study in early 2027, where we hope to see a trend towards slowing of lesion growth comparable to the approved agents at a similar time point. A potential advantage of our systemic approach is the ability to treat bilateral disease, which affects many patients, while avoiding the potentially devastating ocular safety events seen with certain FDA approved agents that are delivered intravitreally. In addition, we are exploring our own intravitreal administration of pozilimab which might also offer safety advantages over currently approved therapies. Moving to NASH.

At the upcoming liver meeting in November, we will present first in human data for our siRNA for CIDEB. This target was discovered by our Regeneron Genetics Center which identified CIDEB's unprecedented ability to protect against liver fat and liver disease through our large scale human genetics database. In the initial data from 40 participants, a single dose was well tolerated and reduced liver fat by approximately 70% on average from baseline in just 12 weeks. Bringing mean liver fat to near or below the upper limit of normal at every dose level tested. This effect was durable through 24 weeks of follow-up and was accompanied by improvements in liver enzymes consistent with reduced liver cell injury.

These results not only clinically validate CIDEB, the discovery from the Regeneron genetic center, but suggest that we have a breakthrough new approach that directly addresses a genetic driver of NASH and could benefit the millions of NASH patients underserved by current approaches. We are working to rapidly advance to registrational trials and look forward to sharing more about this agent at our Next-Generation Roundtable Investor event scheduled for November 10th. Moving to postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome, or POTS, This disease appears to be driven by chronic pathological depletion of intravascular volume. Current treatments include salt and fluid administration, which provide only short term relief. There are no FDA approved therapies, and off label treatments are generally unsatisfactory.

At the American Autonomic Society of Congress, in November, we will be reporting initial results from our phase 2 study. After a single treatment with high dose REGN751 we saw improvements in the 2 key endpoints for this disease. Tachycardia and orthostatic symptoms sustained over 4 weeks from a single dose. These improvements appear to be associated with durable restoration of intravascular volume. We are planning to initiate a potentially registrational study in the first half of next year pending regulatory feedback. And we believe this could be a game changing treatment for a debilitating disease with significant unmet need. Next, turning to ubamatamab. Our MUC16xCD3 bispecific antibody in development for ovarian cancer.

Which was featured in a late breaking plenary session at the International Gynecological Cancer Society meeting. The data presented there along with additional data indicate that ubamatamab monotherapy has an approximately 70% objective response rate with prolonged progression free survival in women with advanced low grade serous ovarian cancer. With an acceptable safety profile and no biomarker selection required. To put this in context, chemotherapy and endocrine therapy have historically delivered response rates below 15% in this setting, and the only approved therapy achieved a 44% response rate but only in the roughly 30 percent of patients with low grade serous ovarian cancers who tumor carry a specific biomarker.

Based on these encouraging early results for uvamatumab, we are enrolling a potentially a registrational cohort in plan to start a confirmatory phase 3 trial in mid 27. Turning now to our larger late stage programs and starting with our BCMAxCD3 bispecific. We believe lynozyfic is differentiated not only by the efficacy demonstrated in late-line multiple myeloma, but also by our development strategy. Which creates important new opportunities in first and second line settings and even in premalignant disease. With pivotal readouts beginning next year. In 2027, we expect initial results from our confirmatory trial of lynozyfic monotherapy versus standard of care in patients with multiple myeloma who received at least 1 prior line of therapy.

In 2028, we expect initial results from our first line study in transplant-ineligible patients as well as from our lynozyfic carfilzomib combination study in patients who received at least 1 prior line of therapy. We are also enrolling potentially a registrational cohort in second line light chain amyloidosis and plan to start a phase 3 study in first line light chain amyloidosis by early 2027. In addition, we are actively enrolling a phase 3 trial in high risk smoldering myeloma. We also have a differentiated development strategy for odronextumab. Our CD20xCD3 bispecific. We have a regulatory application under FDA review for relapsed/refractory diffuse large b cell lymphoma a February 2027 target action date.

Importantly, we expect results in 2028 from our fully enrolled phase 3 study of odronextumab monotherapy in first line follicular lymphoma. Which could provide these patients who have high unmet need with the first bispecific and chemo free immunotherapy options. Moving to anticoagulation. For factor 11 inhibition, we continue to favor our antibody approach over small molecules because antibodies may enable more potent and specific inhibition with the potential to improve antithrombotic activity without increasing bleeding risk or introducing off target safety issues. Our program features cinvasabur, our catalytic domain antibody, and ablasimab, our A2 domain antibody. I am pleased to report that all but 1 of the planned phase 3 studies are now enrolling patients.

These studies span venous thromboembolism prevention after total knee replacement, stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation, cancer associated thrombosis, peripheral artery disease, and most recently, venous thromboembolism prevention in patients with peripherally inserted central catheters. 1 remaining phase 3 study yet to initiate in secondary stroke prevention is expected to begin enrollment by year end. We expect pivotal results from our knee replacement program starting next year with other pivotal studies expected to read out in 2028 and beyond. Turning to olatorepatide, our dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist, in license from Hansoh. Recently, Hansoh presented encouraging efficacy, safety, and tolerability data from their phase 3 trial in patients with obesity in China.

At the European Association for the Study of Diabetes Conference. We look forward to starting our global phase 3 program which is differentiated by our ability to coformulate olatorepatide with Praluent, our PCSK 9 antibody. We believe this could provide an important new treatment option for the many patients with obesity and type 2 diabetes whose comorbidities also suffer from hyper cholesterolemia and increased cardiovascular risk. And we plan to begin registrational studies of this combination next year. As Len discussed, we recently announced an expansion of our alliance with Sanofi.

Building on the success of Dupixent and the validation of the IL 4 and IL 13 pathways as key drivers of type 2 inflammation, The alliance is advancing Regeneron's 4 fully human VelocImmune-derived long acting antibodies and bispecifics. These candidates are designed to preserve Dupixent like efficacy and safety while enabling substantially less frequent dosing. All 4 candidates avoid the heavy engineering that tends to compromise biopharmaceutical properties will raise the risk of anti drug Our candidates which are fully human, and non engineered, also share important molecular properties. So learnings from 1 should carry over to the others and potentially support an expedited development.

Our first in human trial for our lead IL 13 antibody, which has a target dosing interval of every 3 to 6 months, is currently enrolling with a patients with atopic dermatitis. With registrational trials expected to begin in late 2027 and 2020. 3 additional programs a long-acting IL-13 bispecific a long-acting antibody to IL 4 receptor alpha, and an IL 4 ligand antibody are expected to enter the clinic next year. Relevant to these programs, I want to remind. I wanna end by reminding you that we have previously shared early clinical results for a BCMAxCD3 bispecific in combination with Dupixent in severe food allergy.

These results strongly supported our hypothesis that food allergies could potentially be cured by rapidly and completely depleting plasma cells which produce immunoglobulins including the allergy causing IgEs and then continuously suppressing the return of IgE antibodies by blocking IL 4 and IL 13. While the BCMAxCD3 eliminates plasma cells producing all classes of immunoglobulins, we have invented a new bispecific antibody that selectively eliminates only the IgE producing and allergy-causing plasma cells. We plan to build on our groundbreaking results combining our BCMA bispecific with Dupixent expeditiously pursuing this more targeted approach. With clinical studies of this new bispecific antibodies to start in the first half of 2027.

In summary, we have strong momentum across our broad and diverse pipeline that we believe that has the potential to change the practice of medicine across many diseases with high unmet need. With that, let me turn it over to Marion.

Marion McCourt:Thank you, George. Our third quarter results reflect strong commercial execution across our portfolio with our largest brands achieving new all time highs in net sales, Our team is also focused on recent and upcoming launches with Palovarotene now approved in The US for ultra rare FOP, and we are preparing for the November PDUFA date for cemdisiran in generalized myasthenia gravis Starting with Dupixent, which continues to deliver transformative benefits to patients across 9 Type 2 inflammatory diseases with more than 1.5 million patients currently treated worldwide In the U.S., DUPIXENT remains the most prescribed branded biologic among dermatologists, pulmonologists, allergists, and ENTs. Third quarter worldwide net sales of $6.5 billion reflecting 35% growth on a constant currency basis.

US net sales grew 40% year over year to $5.1 billion driven by continued growth across all indications and age groups, as well as favorable gross to net adjustments as reported by Sanofi. DUPIXENT is the leading biologic across our blockbuster indications of atopic dermatitis, asthma, nasal polyps, and eosinophilic esophagitis. supported by its best in class clinical efficacy and safety profile. Uptake is also strong in our more recently launched indications of COPD, prurigo nodularis, chronic spontaneous urticaria, bullous pemphigoid, and allergic fungal rhinosinusitis. With continued growth in new to brand prescriptions. With significant opportunity for future growth across all 9 indications, Dupixent is well positioned over both the near and long term.

Additionally, we are excited about the recently announced expansion of the Regeneron Sanofi alliance and to continue building on the strong foundation we have laid together with Dupixent. Turning to our retinal franchise. In the third quarter, combined EYLEA HD and EYLEA U. S. Net sales were $1.1 billion down 1% compared to last year. With EYLEA HD now comprising nearly 2/3 of the franchise net sales. Third quarter EYLEA HD net sales in The U.S. were $699 million up 62% versus prior year. These results demonstrate strong physician unit demand, which grew 20% from the second quarter.

This growth is driven by the ongoing benefit of recent label enhancements which have increased adoption and broadened use of EYLEA HD across the spectrum of retinal practices physicians increasingly recognize EYLEA HD as the best in class product in the anti VEGF category based on its efficacy, safety and durability. EYLEA U. S. Net sales were $400 million for the quarter, a 41% decrease versus the prior year. Sequential physician unit demand declined by a high single digit percentage compared to the second quarter with this decline partially offset by favorable gross to net adjustments. Both EYLEA HD and EYLEA benefited modestly from the timing of end-of-quarter shipments.

Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, we expect continued EYLEA HD momentum with sequential growth of approximately 10%, partially offset by ongoing pricing pressure resulting in full year net sales growth of over 50% compared with 2025. For EYLEA, we expect a sequential demand decline in the low- to mid-teens in the fourth quarter. Overall, the franchise remains in a strong position despite increasing competition from additional 2-milligram biosimilar launches, and we look forward to potential FDA approval of EYLEA HD prefilled syringe to help sustain EYLEA HD momentum in 2027 and beyond.

Turning to Libtayo, which delivered worldwide net sales of $550 million up 51% year over year on a constant currency basis. and U.S. net sales were $396 million up 81%. In non melanoma skin cancer, Libtayo continues its strength as the leading immunotherapy In The US, the recent approval in adjuvant CSCC is helping to drive growth and is changing the treatment paradigm. Libtayo remains the only NCCN category 1 preferred immunotherapy for eligible patients, and ongoing formulary wins are driving increased usage. In non small cell lung cancer, Libtayo remains the second most prescribed IO as physicians increasingly recognize its strong clinical profile.

We continue to build on Libtayo's strong momentum and enhancing the patient experience through extended dosing and shorter infusion times across all approved indications. We recently received a positive CHMP opinion for every 6-week dosing for Libtayo along with an infusion time as short as 15 minutes An SBLA for this updated dosing regimen is under review with the FDA with a decision expected by March 2027. We expect continued growth for Libtayo as we gain incremental share in lung cancer and drive uptake in adjuvant CSCC. On lynozyfic in multiple myeloma, physician feedback on the currently approved late line setting remains positive based on lynozyfic's differentiating efficacy and safety profiles lower hospitalization requirements, and convenient dosing.

Despite its strong profile, we expect lynozyfic growth to remain modest as we work to advance into earlier lines of therapy. We are also building Regeneron's rare disease portfolio, patients with significant unmet need. Evkeeza continues to grow in its third year on the market with US net sales of $55 million up 28% versus the prior year. We have also expanded our portfolio with the recent launches of Otoferlin for genetic hearing loss, and Palovarotene for FOP. Initial progress for both brands is promising and we look forward to helping patients suffering from these devastating diseases Finally, in neurology, we are preparing for the potential launch of cemdisiran in generalized myasthenia gravis, which has a November PDUFA date.

We see significant commercial opportunity for Cemdisiran based on 3 key factors. Its novel siRNA modality, rapid onset and durable efficacy without the waning treatment effect observed with many other approved therapies, and convenient 4x per year subcutaneous dosing. In closing, our third quarter results reflect strong commercial capability across therapeutic areas. We have built an effective commercial infrastructure that enables us to execute across both in-line brands and new launches, As Len mentioned earlier, our commercialization platform currently spans nearly every relevant specialty, and this market experience positions us well for the many potential new products from our pipeline.

Whether a common or rare disease medicine specialty, or internal medicine prescriber, medical or pharmacy benefit product, we are confident in the capabilities of our commercial organization in both the near and long-term. With that, I will turn the call over to Christopher.

Christopher R. Fenimore:Thank you, Marion. My comments today on Regeneron's financial results and outlook will be on a non GAAP basis unless otherwise noted. Regeneron delivered a strong third quarter, once again reaching double digit growth on both the top and bottom line driven by some sustained momentum across our key growth drivers and solid execution throughout the business. Third quarter total revenue increased 36% from the prior year to $5.1 billion driven primarily by higher Sanofi collaboration revenue, along with strong growth from both Libtayo and EYLEA HD.

Third quarter diluted net income per share grew 70% to $20.07 on net income of $2.2 billion Beginning with the Sanofi collaboration, third quarter collaboration revenues reached an all time high of $2.7 billion including $2.6 billion from our share of collaboration profits. Our share of profits increased 77% versus the prior year primarily driven by continued Dupixent net sales growth and the repayment of the Sanofi development balance, which was completed in the second quarter. Consequently, in the third quarter, we recorded our full share of collaboration profits for the first time. Under the recently amended antibody collaboration, Regeneron and Sanofi will share equally the development and commercialization costs of 4 next-generation antibodies.

Since R&D costs will be co funded as they are incurred, there will be no R&D development balance. Global profits from these antibodies will also be shared 50/50 while the existing economic terms for Dupixent and Kevzara remain unchanged. Regeneron expects to record the full $1 billion upfront payment as Sanofi collaboration revenue in the fourth quarter with any future milestone payments recognized in full in the period achieved. Moving to Bayer. Third quarter net sales of EYLEA 8 mg and EYLEA outside the U.S. were $643 million, inclusive of $384 million of EYLEA 8 mg sales. Total buyer collaboration revenue was $267 million, of which $212 million related to our share of net profits outside the U.S.

Other revenues in the third quarter increased 57% year over year to $310 million, including $253 million from our share of ARCALYST profits and Ilaris royalties. Third quarter Ilaris royalty revenue included an approximately $60 million cumulative catch up adjustment reflecting the application of the highest royalty tier on year to date sales. This cumulative catch up will not recur in the fourth quarter. Now to our operating expenses. Third quarter R and D expense was $1.7 billion, driven by continued advancement of our broad clinical pipeline as well as the timing of related clinical manufacturing. Third quarter SG&A was $588 million, an increase of 9% year over year reflecting investments across our commercial organization and broader business.

Our third quarter effective tax rate was 15%. The year over year increase was primarily due to a shift in the geographic mix of our pretax income driven by higher Sanofi collaboration revenue. Regeneron generated $2.9 billion of free cash flow through the first 9 months of 2026, and ended the quarter with $16.2 billion of cash and marketable securities net of debt. In the first 9 months of 2026, we deployed nearly $3 billion across share repurchases, business development, and dividends. This included $2.3 billion to repurchase 3.2 million shares. We expect full year share repurchases to total approximately $3 billion. And as of September 30, we had $2.2 billion remaining under our repurchase authorization. Moving to guidance.

We made modest refinements to our 2026 financial guidance as we enter the last quarter of the year. A full summary of our guidance can be found in our earnings press release published earlier this morning. As we look to 2027, Len and George discussed the meaningful progress we are making across our innovative pipeline. We expect to advance multiple large registrational programs in myeloma, anticoagulation, obesity, and emerging mid stage opportunities with significant revenue potential such as our programs in POTS and nearly 15 Phase III trials, We believe these investments can create substantial long term value. To support this progress, we currently expect 2027 R&D expense to increase by a mid teens percentage compared with 2026.

Regarding our 2027 effective tax rate, we expect approximately 100 to 200 basis points of upward pressure relative to 2026 consistent with our prior long term tax rate commentary. Finally, turning to the new BARDA agreement for Inmazep, Beginning in late 2027, we expect to supply additional treatment doses to the US government through 2031. Therefore, we do not anticipate recording any revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026 for Inmazeb. In conclusion, we delivered another outstanding quarter and remain well positioned to invest in our differentiated pipeline delivering important medicines to patients and create durable long term value for shareholders. With that, I will pass the call back to Ryan.

Yancopoulos:Well, the other approach is to NASH and reducing liver fat are all somewhat indirect in that they are not directly addressing the fundamental genetic pathway that is underlying or driving this disease.
